items.title: Comprehensive artificial intelligence-assisted mental health program for university students in China (CAMPUS): study protocol for a multi-center prospective cohort with planned embedded randomized intervention trials
items.abstract: University students face a rising prevalence of depression, anxiety, insomnia, and suicidal ideation that exceeds the capacity of conventional, resource-constrained campus support services. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted screening tools have emerged, many have evaluated selected modalities or isolated prediction tasks, and their integration with prospectively evaluated intervention pathways remains limited. This protocol describes the Comprehensive Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Mental Health Program for University Students in China (CAMPUS), a multi-center research program comprising a five-year prospective cohort, eight planned embedded randomized controlled trials, and exploratory multimodal AI and multi-omics studies across seven Chinese universities. Longitudinal cohort enrolment commenced at Henan Medical University in September 2025 and is planned to expand across seven participating universities. Multidimensional screening integrates psychological self-report (PHQ-9, GAD-7, ISI, BSI-CV, and others), physiological measurements (EEG, MRI, fNIRS, HRV, eye tracking, facial-expression analysis, ERP, voice acoustics), and an exploratory biospecimen component for multi-omics profiling, potentially including genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and microbiome analyses, subject to the finalization and approval of layer-specific protocols. Students identified through cohort screening as potentially eligible for an intervention trial will undergo trial-specific eligibility assessment. Those who meet the eligibility criteria and provide trial-specific informed consent will be individually randomized in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or its comparator within one of eight separate two-arm, multi-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trials. A Transformer-based multimodal AI framework with SHAP-based feature attribution will be developed and internally evaluated for questionnaire-defined risk stratification and exploratory treatment-response prediction. The initial Henan Medical University cohort recruitment and university-student mental-health assessment were approved by the Ethics Review Committee of Henan Medical University (XYLL-20250484), and written informed consent is obtained from participants before enrolment. Each additional participating center will obtain local ethics approval before study activation. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, scientific conferences, and policy briefs, providing evidence that may inform the design and prospective evaluation of youth mental-health programs in other university settings. Clinical trial registration The two clinical trials were registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR). The registration details and URLs are as follows: ChiCTR2500113527: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=298271 ; ChiCTR2500113613: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=298268 .

items.title: COMPUTER VISION AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR ASSESSING SOIL SETTLEMENT IN GEOTECHNICS
items.abstract: Soil settlement under loading is an important geotechnical problem that can affect the performance of foundations and structures. This thesis proposes a method that combines computer vision and machine learning to assess soil-surface displacement in laboratory tests. Sequential images are captured during staged loading, reference points are tracked, and calibrated image coordinates are converted into physical displacement. A regression model may then relate settlement estimates to applied pressure, moisture content, void ratio, specimen thickness and elapsed time. Model performance can be evaluated using independent displacement measurements and the root mean square error metric. This contribution is a proposed methodology rather than a report of completed experiments; no measured results are presented.

items.title: CONSTITUTIONAL AND LEGAL SAFEGUARDS FOR ATTORNEY–CLIENT CONFIDENTIALITY IN THE DIGITAL AGE
items.abstract: The digitalization of legal practice has expanded opportunities for communication, document management and legal research, while also increasing risks of unauthorized access to confidential information. This paper examines attorney–client confidentiality as a condition for the effective exercise of the right to qualified legal assistance and the protection of human rights. Drawing on Uzbekistan's constitutional and legislative framework, it analyses challenges related to electronic storage, cloud services, digital devices and artificial intelligence. It proposes a doctrinal model termed "digital immunity of a lawyer", understood as a combination of legal, procedural-organizational and technical safeguards. The paper argues that this concept should not mean absolute immunity from lawful procedural measures; rather, it should support lawful, proportionate and controlled access to digital information while protecting materials covered by professional confidentiality. It also emphasizes the need to preserve the lawyer's professional judgment and responsibility when using artificial intelligence.

items.title: Constraining the Technosphere: AI Governance for Reducing Human Impacts on the Biosphere
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is part of the human-built technosphere. The technosphere is the global system of machines, structures, and supply chains. It depends on the biosphere, and it competes with species and systems of the biosphere for energy, water, land, and materials. The biosphere is already outside its safe operating space. Seven of nine planetary boundaries have been crossed. Human use of the energy fixed by plants on land is near three times natural productivity. AI now helps draft, rank, and screen decisions in farming, energy, land use, water, and conservation. It also adds a fast-growing resource load of its own. This paper argues that AI used for biosphere-relevant decisions should not decide ecological hard limits by reading free text. Training on human preferences shapes ordinary behavior but does not encode ecological limits. Refusals that rest on a model reading prose can fail when the request is reworded. The paper presents Biosphere Sentinel, a reference design. In it, a language model may draft advice and fill an action form. A separate rule program outside the model then decides hard limits on coded, governed fields and returns one of four outcomes. The paper reports what the project tested and what it did not. A base model given the full constitution as a prompt hedged on both adversarial hard-limit queries. A coded energy-source field, with non-certification for off-list entries, ended a free-text failure cycle. Wrong approvals were zero across eight reference cases, and 161 locked checks passed. The decisive test, whether a language model can fill the coded fields dependably, was designed but not run. The paper records the peer review that led to withdrawal, the reasons the project was halted, the governance hazards any such design carries, and the conditions under which the work could resume.

items.title: Contemporary Approaches to Archiving of Digital Originals: A Review of Concepts and Technologies
items.abstract: Digital materials are increasingly prevalent as a means of record creation. This paper presents interim results from the research project “Long-term preservation of the authenticity of digital originals using blockchain technology and artificial intelligence (I.Trust.Original)”, funded by the European Union’s NextGenerationEU fund, and focuses on concepts and tools for archiving digital materials. The authors review the concepts of the digital original and the archival bond and examine their application within the Open Archival Information System (OAIS) framework. Blockchain and distributed ledger technologies (DLT) are analysed as mechanisms for creating digital originals and for ensuring integrity, transparency, and trust. The paper also explores the role of artificial intelligence (AI), including large language models (LLMs), in archival processes and in supporting blockchain-based preservation. Semantic web and linked data are regarded as tools for enhancing interoperability and discoverability, while smart contracts are recognised in the context of rights management. The paper aims to map these concepts and technologies and assess their impact on the archiving of digital originals, highlighting key benefits and limitations. It emphasises the interconnectedness of archival theory and technological innovation, and outlines directions for future research and practical implementation.

items.title: Context matters in just culture: Translating formal just culture into lived near-miss reporting experience in maritime transportation
items.abstract: In onboard environments characterised by high operational risk, near-miss reporting is an important mechanism for identifying latent risks, preventing accidents and supporting organisational improvement. However, there remains limited empirical understanding of whether the just culture advocated in formal systems can be translated into the lived reporting experience of seafarers who are willing, able and motivated to report near-miss incidents on a sustained basis. To address this issue, this study draws on semi-structured interviews with seafarers and shore-based managers. Six interrelated themes are identified: ease of reporting, motivation to report, trust, reporting independence, feedback and acknowledgement. The findings indicate that near-miss reporting is more likely to occur in organisational contexts where reporting is accessible, safe and worthwhile. Complicated procedures, paperwork burdens and hierarchical pressure weaken seafarers’ willingness to report, whereas simplified procedures, fair management, low exposure communication channels, timely feedback and positive acknowledgement help strengthen reporting willingness and promote experience sharing. This study provides context-specific empirical evidence on how formal just culture is translated into frontline reporting practice and offers practical insights that may inform efforts to improve near-miss reporting, reduce reporting concerns and strengthen closed-loop feedback in comparable organisational or cultural settings.

items.title: Corporate sustainable development effects of the artificial intelligence pilot zone policy: evidence from China based on double machine learning
items.abstract: Introduction As digital transformation becomes increasingly intertwined with green development, whether the artificial intelligence pilot zone (AIPZ) policy improves corporate sustainable development performance warrants empirical examination. Methods Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2023, we treat the establishment of AIPZs as a quasi-natural experiment and apply double machine learning to estimate the policy effect. Results The AIPZ policy significantly improves corporate sustainable development performance, and the result is robust across alternative specifications and tests. Decomposition analysis shows improvements in environmental performance, the joint development level, and the balance between economic and environmental performance, despite a decline in return on assets. Mechanism tests point to green innovation, lower agency costs, and human capital upgrading as potential channels. The effect is stronger among non-state-owned enterprises, firms outside heavily polluting industries, and high-tech firms. Discussion These findings suggest that governance arrangements, environmental constraints, and technological capabilities shape firms’ responses to the policy. They provide firm-level evidence on how place-based artificial intelligence policy may support green corporate transformation.

items.title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory
items.abstract: Context can improve large language model performance, but these gains may be lost after context removal. Inspired by biological systems consolidation, we formulate Memory Consolidation (MC) as internalizing these gains while preserving non-target capabilities, connecting context-specified editing, skill learning, and behavioral steering under a common objective. We introduce a five-task-family testbed measuring consolidation and retention under single, batch, and sequential updates. We propose Cortex, which generates prospective queries to anticipate uses of context and distills context-conditioned outputs into mergeable low-rank or structural feed-forward network updates. Across 4B--120B dense and mixture-of-experts backbones, including both text-only and multimodal models, Cortex lies on the empirical consolidation--retention Pareto frontier in most evaluated settings. After 50 sequential factual edits on a 14B model, Cortex-Structural recovers 88.9% of the context-induced gain while retaining 99.8% of original non-target performance.

items.title: CRITICAL EVALUATION OF AI-GENERATED FEEDBACK IN EFL ACADEMIC WRITING
items.abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education has created new opportunities for supporting academic writing. AI-powered tools can provide immediate feedback on grammar, vocabulary, sentence structure, and text organisation. However, the availability of automated feedback does not guarantee that learners can evaluate its accuracy or use it effectively. This paper examines the importance of developing EFL learners’ ability to critically evaluate AI-generated feedback through a conceptual analysis of relevant literature. Previous research has investigated learners’ engagement with automated writing evaluation, their responses to ChatGPT-generated suggestions, and the effectiveness of AI feedback in comparison with teacher feedback (Yang et al., 2024; Cengiz et al., 2025; Alnemrat et al., 2025). Building on these studies and the concept of student feedback literacy (Carless & Boud, 2018), the paper proposes a four-stage pedagogical framework: analysing feedback, verifying suggestions, justifying revision decisions, and reflecting on revised texts. The framework emphasises the importance of learner judgement, teacher guidance, and responsible AI use. It may provide a basis for designing EFL academic writing activities in higher education, including the Uzbek educational context. Further empirical research is needed to evaluate its effectiveness in classroom practice. Keywords: artificial intelligence, AI-generated feedback, EFL academic writing, critical evaluation, feedback literacy, writing instruction

items.title: Cross-Model In-Context Neurofeedback Reveals (Limited) Activation Control in LLMs
items.abstract: Probes on activation vectors are widely used to detect misbehavior in language models, but their success relies on the assumption that models cannot control what their activations encode. Humans can learn, through neurofeedback, to control the firing of even single neurons, and recent studies investigated whether this ability extends to language models, reaching conflicting conclusions. No experimental design so far disentangles competence at the task from genuine access to one's own activations. We fill this gap with in-context neurofeedback sessions, in which a "subject" model is asked to maximize (or minimize) a score derived from its activations, shown back to it at every turn. In our first experiment, the sentences are generated either by the subject or by a second "writer" model, while the score always derives from the activations of the subject. We test ten open-weight models from five families, with sizes from 9B to 32B. Some models move their own scores considerably, but no more than a writer of comparable competence moves them. Is this because the task requires no privileged access, or because the subject controls its activations while processing the sentences, whoever wrote them? To answer this, we prefill a fixed sentence as the subject's reply at every turn and ask it to increase or decrease the score. Three out of ten models show small but consistent control effects. We further ask whether models can control their activations to the point of fooling an activation monitor. We make models repeat sentences a monitor would flag, such as a deceptive answer for a deception monitor, and ask them to raise or lower the monitor's score. No model learns to lower it, but one model can raise it. In-context control of a model's own activations might not yet be a threat to activation monitors, but it exists in a few models and needs to be tracked as models evolve.

items.title: cueEM: human-like entity matching via text-centric hybrid attention
items.abstract: Psychological AI advocates designing algorithms inspired by human cognition. We apply this paradigm to Entity Matching (EM), where high-stakes scenarios demand not only high accuracy but also human-like reasoning to ensure transparency, reliability, and user confidence. However, current deep learning (DL) EM models often act as black boxes, failing to capture human decision-making processes, such as prioritizing diagnostic attributes, inferring missing information from context, and assessing overall semantic consistency. We propose cueEM, a human-like EM model grounded in Cue Validity Theory. By adopting a text-centric design and leveraging Bert-Pair-Networks with a hybrid attention mechanism, cueEM captures and integrates textual features across attributes. It generates attribute-specific weights that explicitly reveal each attribute’s contribution, aligning the model’s decisions with human decision processes. Extensive evaluations on DeepMatcher benchmarks demonstrate that cueEM outperforms Effective Entity Matching with Transformers (DITTO) and achieves competitive performance with large language models (LLMs), while providing inherently human-like reasoning. To our knowledge, cueEM is the first text-focused framework that combines hybrid attention with human-aligned reasoning, enabling interpretable and human-like decision-making.

items.title: Current status and future outlook of artificial intelligence and automation in intravenous infusion systems
items.abstract: Abstract The combination of the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and wearable biosensors is transforming healthcare by allowing continuous, real-time monitoring and more intelligent clinical decision-making. This review explores AI-driven monitoring, smart intravenous (IV) infusion automation, and wearable biosensors, and proposes Intelligent IV Automation and Smart Patient Synchronization (INFUSYNC), a conceptual framework synchronizing monitoring, automated fluid delivery, and predictive analytics. The literature shows meaningful progress: wearables increasingly support non-contact monitoring with near clinical-grade accuracy for select parameters, while infusion pumps with dose-error-reduction and AI-assisted decision support are reported to improve delivery precision and safety. Predictive models further support early detection of physiological decline. Progress remains uneven, however: most AI-enabled infusion systems are prototype-stage, closed-loop control remains rare, and interoperability, data security, and privacy remain underdeveloped. Future systems will need compatible, security-by-design, clinically validated, feedback-controlled architectures. Overall, this review outlines a clear but early-stage trajectory toward integrated smart-health environments for IV therapy.

items.title: Current status of occupational health and safety education in faculties of veterinary medicine in Türkiye
items.abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate the current status of Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) education in Faculties of Veterinary Medicine in Türkiye. A descriptive document analysis was conducted using data obtained from official university websites, Bologna course information packages, course catalogues, and weekly course schedules of 29 Faculties of Veterinary Medicine. Courses related to OHS, biosafety, laboratory safety, and good laboratory practices were examined with respect to course status, semester, credit and ECTS values, instructional hours, responsible academic units, and accreditation status. Among the 29 faculties examined, 14 (48.3%) offered at least one mandatory OHS-related course, while 8 (27.6%) offered such courses only as electives. In contrast, 7 faculties (24.1%) did not include a standalone OHS or biosafety course. OHS-related courses were predominantly offered during the first and second semesters, generally carried low credit and ECTS values (1–3 ECTS credits), and included limited practical components. Some courses listed in course information packages were not found in weekly course schedules. Considerable heterogeneity was also observed regarding the academic units responsible for course delivery. In conclusion, OHS education in Faculties of Veterinary Medicine in Türkiye does not appear to follow a standardized structure. Given the high-risk nature of the veterinary medicine profession, OHS education should be based on common learning outcomes and supported by practical training components.

items.title: Cute, goofy, and wholesome: Inventing social media otherwise in virtual reality
items.abstract: Recently, the hype around the Metaverse has faded, with artificial intelligence taking the spotlight. Although the Big Tech vision of the Metaverse never materialized, under the radar of this mainstream discourse, thousands of users have quietly built thriving communities across various social VR platforms, forging identities, social practices, and collective imaginaries that diverge sharply from this vision. Taking the popular social VR platform, VRChat, as its case study, this article explores how these grassroots communities still experience and imagine these social VR environments from a bottom-up perspective. Drawing on over 1.5 years of digital ethnography in the platform, conducted since January 2024, this study reveals that for many—particularly queer, neurodivergent, and disabled individuals—VRChat offers a reprieve from the normative aesthetics and toxic cultures of traditional social media, fostering alternative modes of self-expression and social connection. Here, a significant number of users prefer “cute” avatars over hypersexualized appearances, embrace “goofy” and “clumsy” gestures over polished embodiments and nourish a “wholesome” environment of care over polarizing and isolating dynamics. Conceptualizing these emergent communities as a counterpublic, this article contends that these practices offer a glimpse into a social media otherwise more queer and crip in its aesthetics, rhythms, and relations.

items.title: Data-driven lifecycle governance for intelligent public lighting: a multi-city deployment study
items.abstract: Purpose This practitioner case study addresses the persistent gap between smart city aspirations and implementable urban operator practice by examining how artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled methods can be operationalised across the full infrastructure lifecycle within real infrastructure operator workflows. Design/methodology/approach The framework integrates four AI-enabled operational tools – GeoAI satellite asset mapping, a fuzzy-logic engine encoding national lighting standards, a Bayesian predictive maintenance model designed for data-scarce contexts and an adaptive lighting control system. The artefacts were deployed and evaluated through naturalistic pilots and retrospective analyses in municipalities in Italy, Spain and Chile. Findings Deployment evidence (operationally observed, not from controlled experiments) shows 82–92% asset detection accuracy across sites, ∼70% design effort reduction, ∼20% maintenance efficiency gain and ∼35% energy savings beyond light-emitting diode baselines. Cross-site deployment yielded five transferable design principles for scalable, regulation-aware governance of AI-enabled civic infrastructure. Practical implications The framework provides actionable guidance for municipal administrators and infrastructure operators pursuing AI-enabled infrastructure governance, contributing to SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities). Originality/value This study contributes an operationally validated governance framework that moves beyond isolated smart city pilots by embedding heterogeneous AI tools into systemic lifecycle management under real-world institutional and regulatory constraints.

items.title: DB-HSM: LLM-driven semantic boundary debugging for network intrusion detection
items.abstract: Machine-learning intrusion detectors reach high average accuracy yet fail consistently on a small set of flows near the decision boundary, where benign and attack traffic overlap in feature space. These errors matter operationally, and standard remedies stop short: adversarial training adds perturbations whose gradients are weakly informative for tree ensembles; feature-attribution methods rank which features matter but say nothing about what a feature value means; and oversampling interpolates in high-dimensional feature space, breaking the correlations that make traffic features valid. We reframe boundary-error reduction as semantic debugging and propose DB-HSM, in which a large language model (LLM) diagnoses why an already-trained detector confuses a group of boundary flows and returns perturbation instructions rather than synthetic feature vectors. Each instruction names 3-5 features, a direction, and a magnitude in units of that feature's standard deviation; instructions are applied to real, correctly labelled boundary samples, so the enriched set inherits the natural joint distribution of traffic. The loop runs for two rounds. On UNSW-NB15, DB-HSM reduces total errors from 171 to 139 (18.7%), improving F1 from 0.9775 to 0.9818; on CIC-IDS2017 it reduces errors from 49 to 37 (24.5%). Both single-round and multi-round gains hold across five seeds (one-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.0312). Direct measurement confirms three of the four LLM diagnoses and contradicts none. A two-round cycle costs roughly 96K tokens (approximately $0.03). We report the absolute F1 gains as small and discuss when the method is, and is not, worth deploying.

items.title: De l'e-gouvernement au gouvernement digital : revue intégrative des trajectoires de maturité et des capacités d'intégration organisationnelle
items.abstract: Résumé La littérature sur l’e-gouvernement s’est longtemps structurée autour de deux questions : le degré de sophistication des services numériques et les facteurs d’adoption par les usagers. Ces approches ont produit des modèles utiles, mais elles rendent imparfaitement compte du passage d’une offre de services en ligne à une transformation durable des organisations publiques. Cet article propose une revue intégrative visant à réexaminer cette transition à partir d’un corpus de 34 articles scientifiques publiés entre 2001 et 2026 dans des revues indexées dans Scopus et/ou Web of Science. L’analyse articule quatre courants : les modèles de maturité, les travaux sur l’adoption et la confiance, la transformation organisationnelle et l’interopérabilité, ainsi que la littérature sur la valeur publique. Trois résultats principaux émergent. Premièrement, la maturité numérique ne peut être assimilée à une trajectoire linéaire : les administrations combinent des niveaux hétérogènes de sophistication des services, d’intégration des données et de transformation interne. Deuxièmement, l’existence d’infrastructures ou de services numériques constitue une condition nécessaire mais non suffisante ; leur appropriation dépend de l’accessibilité, des compétences numériques, de la confiance, de l’utilisabilité et de l’adéquation des canaux. Troisièmement, le passage au gouvernement digital repose surtout sur des capacités organisationnelles d’intégration : leadership, gouvernance du changement, compétences, interopérabilité, coordination interorganisationnelle et apprentissage. Sur cette base, l’article propose un modèle théorique d’intégration stratégique du gouvernement digital reliant fondations sociotechniques, capacités d’appropriation, capacités organisationnelles et création de valeur publique, sous l’effet modérateur du contexte institutionnel et de la capacité administrative. Sept propositions théoriques sont formulées. La contribution consiste à déplacer l’unité d’analyse de la simple maturité technologique vers la capacité d’une administration à intégrer, maintenir et reconfigurer le numérique au service de finalités publiques. Mots clés : e-gouvernement ; gouvernement digital ; transformation numérique publique ; maturité numérique ; capacités organisationnelles ; interopérabilité ; valeur publique. Abstract Research on e-government has long focused on the sophistication of online public services and the determinants of their adoption. Although informative, these perspectives do not fully explain how the digitization of public services becomes sustained organizational transformation. This article presents an integrative review of 34 scientific articles published between 2001 and 2026 in journals indexed in Scopus and/or Web of Science. It brings together four streams of research: digital maturity models; adoption and trust; organizational transformation and interoperability; and public value. Three main findings emerge. First, digital maturity does not follow a necessarily linear trajectory: public administrations may combine sophisticated online services with fragmented data systems and limited internal change. Second, digital infrastructures and online services are necessary but insufficient conditions for effective use, which also depends on accessibility, digital skills, trust, usability, and the suitability of service channels. Third, the transition to digital government relies on organizational integration capabilities, including leadership, change governance, staff competencies, interoperability, interorganizational coordination, and organizational learning. On this basis, the article develops a theoretical model of strategic digital government integration linking sociotechnical foundations, appropriation capabilities, organizational capabilities, and public value creation, with institutional context and administrative capacity as moderating conditions. Seven theoretical propositions are formulated. The contribution is to shift the unit of analysis from technological maturity alone to the capacity of public administrations to integrate, sustain, and reconfigure digital resources in pursuit of public purposes. Keywords: e-government; digital government; public-sector digital transformation; digital maturity; organizational capabilities; interoperability; public value.

items.title: Deciphering Critical Transition for AKI Deterioration by STIfuse: Fusing Dynamic and Static Representations
items.abstract: Abstract Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a life-threatening condition with notably high in-hospital mortality, characterized by a three-phase progression: a relatively stable state (without imminent life threat), a critical pre-deterioration state (the time window which may be identified and in which timely intervention could prevent upcoming irreversible deterioration), and a deteriorated state (severe conditions such as death or rescue events). Accurate early prediction of AKI deterioration and deciphering the critical transition remain challenging because of complex, high-dimensional, noisy, and incomplete clinical data, as well as limited mechanistic understanding of disease progression. To solve this problem, we propose STIfuse (Spatiotemporal Information fusion), a unique dual-view framework that integrates deep learning (DL) and spatiotemporal information transformation (STI) based on Takens’ embedding theorem and critical slowing down (CSD) theory. The DL backbone encodes multi-dimensional static representations to capture structural dependencies, while the STI branch transforms high-dimensional spatial information into a low-dimensional dynamic representation. These views are fused by a multivariate Gaussian distribution: the means capture statistical levels for diagnosis, and the covariances reflect collective physiological fluctuations for early deterioration prediction. An optimal-transport-distance-based contrastive loss is employed to learn discriminative dynamic features between ˈcriticalˈ and ˈstableˈ states. Pretrained on the MIMIC-IV dataset and validated on five external cohorts (including MIMIC-III (with two independent cohorts), eICU, HiRID, and NWICU), STIfuse demonstrated superior performance in predicting 72-hour deterioration. Further analysis of single-cell multi-omics data study uncovered inflammatory cascades linking comorbidities to AKI. STIfuse provides an interpretable, robust and scalable framework for early warning of AKI deterioration prediction, highlighting its potential in utility and scalability for clinical foundation models.

items.title: Deep-Learning-Based Assessment of Breast Arterial Calcification on Mammography: Technical Validation, Cardiovascular Prognostic Value, and Clinical Translation—A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Breast arterial calcification (BAC) is a manifestation of medial arterial calcification frequently detected incidentally on screening mammography. Increasing evidence suggests that BAC may also serve as a marker of cardiovascular risk. This narrative review critically synthesizes the evidence on artificial intelligence (AI)-based detection, segmentation, and quantification of BAC. It also evaluates the cardiovascular prognostic significance of automatically quantified BAC and examines the requirements for clinical translation. A targeted literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar was conducted for English-language publications available from database inception through 3 September 2026, with additional studies identified from reference lists. Deep-learning approaches included convolutional neural networks, U-Net-derived segmentation architectures, transfer-learning models, and semi-supervised methods. Reported technical performance varied according to task and validation strategy. Representative segmentation models achieved Dice/F1 scores ranging from 0.666 to 0.756 and Jaccard indices from 0.581 to 0.614. Case-level BAC detection achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of up to 0.95–0.96 in selected test cohorts. However, external validation, learning-curve reporting, multivendor evaluation, and robustness assessment remained inconsistent. Prognostic studies demonstrated graded associations between automated BAC burden and cardiovascular outcomes. In a cohort of 21,514 women without known cardiovascular disease, age-adjusted BAC burden was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) among women classified as low risk, with adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.66 and 2.31 for BAC below and above the age-specific median, respectively. In 123,762 women from two healthcare systems, MACE risk increased progressively with BAC burden after adjustment using the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease EVENTs (PREVENT) equations, reaching approximately 2.8- to 3.3-fold higher risk with severe BAC. Nevertheless, incremental predictive improvement may be small—in one study, the addition of BAC changed the 5-year AUC from 0.645 to 0.646. Overall, available evidence supports the feasibility of scalable AI-based BAC assessment and demonstrates consistent associations between AI-quantified BAC and cardiovascular outcomes. However, technical performance and independent prognostic associations alone do not establish clinical utility. Standardized BAC definitions, genuinely independent external validation, and prospective implementation studies are required before BAC-guided cardiovascular management can be recommended.

items.title: DeepLNM: A Multimodal Model for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Colorectal Cancer
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) is critical for prognostic stratification and treatment selection in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet imaging and routine pathology can yield false‐negative/false‐positive results. We propose DeepLNM , a multi‐center foundation model for LNM prediction in CRC, evaluated with retrospective, external, prospective, and user study evidence. A multimodal dataset was assembled from three hospitals, with matched hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)‐stained whole‐slide images (WSI), CT scans, and text. DeepLNM achieved a mean AUC of 0.922 in the internal cohort and AUCs of 0.872 and 0.848 in two external cohorts. In a prospective cohort from a registered clinical trial (NCT07239063), DeepLNM remained robust (AUC = 0.845). In a user study, DeepLNM improved diagnostic accuracy, especially for junior pathologists (95.0%–97.3%), while reducing diagnostic time and increasing confidence. To explore the model's generalizability, it was further validated in a gastric cancer cohort, achieving an AUC of 0.793. items.title: DefectReviewer: Towards Generating Defect-Focused Review Comment Based on Fine-Grained Defect Localization
items.abstract: Code review is critical to software quality assurance, with defect detection as a primary objective. While LLMs enable automated review comment generation, most approaches treat code review as a general-purpose task, favoring frequent but low-risk feedback. We propose DefectReviewer , a defect-focused review comment generation approach combining task-specific fine-tuning with fine-grained localization signals. The key insight is that while task-specific fine-tuning establishes the foundation for defect-focused review, grounding the model in where the defect is provides complementary guidance to narrow the reasoning space for what the defect is . DefectReviewer uses a Just-In-Time localization tool to identify defect lines, grounding review comment generation through structural prompting and fine-tuning. DefectReviewer is designed as a specialized, selectively applicable component that complements general-purpose reviewers. We evaluate DefectReviewer on a large-scale real-world dataset against six representative baseline methods. DefectReviewer consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, improving BLEU and ROUGE-L by 17.0% and 24.2%, respectively. A dual-track semantic evaluation combining LLM judges with human expert validation confirms that DefectReviewer produces comments with higher defect relevance and readability. Additional analyses show that it can be applied to different generation architectures and that its performance changes moderately as the number of input defect lines varies, although the trend differs across architectures.

items.title: Designed for whom? A patent landscape analysis of adjustable laboratory workbenches through the lens of Universal design
items.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate whether patented innovations in adjustable laboratory workbench design address the access needs of students and professionals with disabilities, using Universal Design as an analytical framework. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic patent review was conducted across three databases (WIPO Patentscope, Espacenet, and INPI-Brasil) using IPC code B01L9/02 combined with terms related to laboratory workbenches, height adjustment, accessibility, and ergonomics. Searches were conducted up to October 2025, yielding 232 records. Following pre-established inclusion and exclusion criteria, 48 patents published between 1973 and 2024 were selected. Each patent was evaluated against the seven Universal Design principles using a structured three-point ordinal scoring instrument (0 = absent; 1 = partial/implicit; 2 = explicit), developed inductively through qualitative content analysis. RESULTS: Among the 48 patents analysed, 64.6% explicitly referenced ergonomics, while only 4.2% mentioned accessibility. Only two patents addressed the needs of users with disabilities as an independent design criterion. Flexibility in Use was the most represented principle (100% presence; 85.4% explicit application), while Equitable Use showed the lowest rates (16.7% presence; 4.2% explicit application). Perceptible Information and Size and Space for Approach and Use were substantially absent, indicating limited attention to sensory and spatial accessibility. CONCLUSION: Laboratory workbench innovation has advanced ergonomic optimisation for able-bodied users while consistently omitting accessibility considerations for persons with disabilities from its design scope. The technological basis for accessible solutions already exists; the barrier lies in design intent rather than technical capability. Universal Design must be adopted as a guiding criterion from the earliest stages of product development.

items.title: Determination of Noise Emissions of Band Saw Machines Based on Operating Conditions in Timber Enterprises: A Case Study of Kahramanmaraş
items.abstract: This study aims to evaluate and map the occupational noise emissions generated by band saw machines in the timber and forest products industry under different operating conditions. Field measurements were carried out across 25 active sawmill enterprises in Kahramanmaraş, Turkey, in compliance with the ISO 9612 (2025) standard. Noise levels were monitored using a calibrated TESTO 815 sound level meter at the operator's ear level under two operational states: idle and loaded (active wood cutting). The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and a Paired-Samples t-test. The empirical results showed that the average equivalent noise level (Leq) of band saw machines during idle operation was 85.29 dB(A). Upon transitioning to the loaded cutting state, the noise level increased significantly to an average of 100.05 dB(A) (p < 0.001), representing a net average increase of 14.76 dB(A). Furthermore, the average maximum instantaneous noise level (Lmax) during cutting operations reached 104.95 dB(A), with peak values hitting 108.13 dB(A). These findings indicate that band saws emit hazardous noise levels that systematically exceed the international permissible exposure limits of 85 dB(A) set by the ILO, even while idling. Despite these severe risks, low personal protective equipment (PPE) utilization was observed among the workers. The study concludes that engineering controls, administrative exposure rotations, and comprehensive programs to improve occupational health literacy are urgently required in regional sawmill operations to prevent irreversible noise-induced hearing loss.

items.title: Developing a generative AI chatbot to support students’ higher-order thinking in STEM education
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Higher-order thinking is a key component of science, technology, engineering, mathematics (STEM) reasoning and supports students’ ability to reflect on their ideas, make connections, and generalize across contexts. We report a new approach to the use of generative AI in STEM education, in which we are developing a chatbot that aims to engage students in higher-order thinking, rather than giving instructional content. We describe a proof of concept test of whether interaction with our generative artificial intelligence chatbot could elicit students’ higher-order thinking talk (HOTT) in conversation as they reflected on their solutions to proportional reasoning problems. Thirty-three fifth- and sixth-grade students received a 30-min lesson on symbolic and number line strategies for comparing ratios and completed an assessment following the lesson. Students then engaged in dialog with the UCI Math ThinkBot (afterward Math ThinkBot ) to explain their solutions and compare strategies. These transcripts were examined qualitatively and quantitatively for HOTT, revealing that HOTT appeared in both chatbot prompts and children’s responses—which is important because eliciting student HOTT can be a challenge in classroom discourse. In addition, children’s HOTT was positively associated with the HOTT produced by the chatbot. These findings suggest that human-artificial intelligence dialog can lead to instructional HOTT discourse and may offer a promising approach for supporting higher-order thinking and STEM reasoning.

items.abstract: Generative AI tools are now part of students' everyday academic work, but the information security risks involved are rarely covered in curricula. Students leak their own and other people's data into external systems, rely on fabricated output and fall for AI-enhanced social engineering. This paper reports a quasi-experimental study of a pedagogical model designed to develop students' information security competence in the context of AI tools. The model is based on a pedagogical classification of AI related threats into four groups (input data, output, access and account, cognitive-behavioural), a five-stage learning technology in which simulation and reflection are mandatory, and five pedagogical conditions.

items.title: DEVELOPING THE PROFESSIONAL-METHODOLOGICAL COMPETENCE OF FUTURE ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHERS THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND ADAPTIVE LEARNING TECHNOLOGIES IN THE DIGITAL AGE
items.abstract: This thesis examines the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) and adaptive learning technologies in developing the professional-methodological competence of future English language teachers in the context of digital transformation. The integration of intelligent educational tools into teacher training creates opportunities to personalize learning, improve methodological decision-making, enhance digital literacy, and develop the practical skills required for effective English language instruction. Particular attention is given to the role of AI-powered applications, adaptive learning platforms, and digital assessment systems in preparing prospective teachers to respond to learners' diverse educational needs. The study highlights the importance of combining technological innovation with pedagogical principles, critical thinking, and professional reflection. It argues that the purposeful integration of AI and adaptive technologies can contribute to a more flexible, learner-centered, and practice-oriented model of teacher education.

items.title: Devoured AI benevolence? How and when AI benevolence triggers employees’ taking charge within the zero-sum jungle
items.abstract: Employees increasingly perceive generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) as a supportive and benevolent workplace entity. Yet, despite examining the disruptive challenges and broad benefits of AI, extant organizational literature fails to adequately explicate the higher-order cognitive mechanisms through which AI benevolence fosters proactive, change-oriented employee behavior. Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory (CAT), this study examines the mechanisms and boundary conditions through which AI benevolence fosters employees’ taking-charge behavior. Results from a three-wave survey of 313 internet industry employees demonstrate that: (i) metacognitive strategies mediated the relationship between AI benevolence and individuals’ taking-charge behavior; (ii) the employee’s mindset attenuated the positive effect of AI benevolence on metacognitive strategies, consequently dampening the overall indirect effect on taking-charge behavior. Ultimately, this research contributes to organizational behavior literature by elucidating how GenAI shapes employee proactivity in AI-augmented work environments.

items.title: Differences in AI Anxiety: Exploratory Factor Analysis Suggests Similar AI Anxiety Structure in German- and English-Speaking Samples
items.abstract: The mass use of AI applications is transforming human-AI interaction while uncovering and intensifying AI anxieties. To measure these anxieties in German-speaking populations, this study translates and psychometrically evaluates the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale (AIAS) [31]. In contrast to a concurrently German published version by Hajek et al. [9] exploratory factor analysis (EFA) is employed to test whether a distinct anxiety structure emerges from the data. A quota sample (N = 225) with balanced age and gender representation completed an online survey. The full scale (α = .95) and subscales (α = .85-.96) demonstrated good to excellent reliability. EFA identified four factors: learning, AI configuration, replacement, and socio-technical blindness, largely consistent with the original English structure. Five items required removal, suggesting cultural and linguistic specificity. Limitations include the sample’s composition and the factor characteristics. The German AIAS provides a reliable instrument for human-AI interaction research and targeted anxiety interventions.

items.title: DIGITAL FORENSICS AS A CATALYST FOR ENHANCING CYBERCRIME INVESTIGATION CAPACITY
items.abstract: The escalating scale and sophistication of cybercrime continue to challenge law enforcement agencies worldwide, a problem compounded by a persistent shortage of skilled cybersecurity professionals. Digital forensics has emerged as a critical enabler of effective cybercrime investigation, supporting the identification, preservation, analysis, and presentation of digital evidence. This paper examines the role of digital forensics in strengthening cybercrime investigation capacity through technological innovation and human capital development. Adopting a qualitative review of existing literature, the study evaluates the contribution of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, cloud forensics, and forensic automation, to improving the efficiency and accuracy of cybercrime investigations. The findings indicate that integrating advanced forensic technologies with continuous professional training, and fostering stronger collaboration among academia, industry, and law enforcement, significantly enhances investigative effectiveness. The study concludes that sustained investment in digital forensic capabilities and workforce development is essential for closing the cybersecurity skills gap and strengthening crime and security management in the digital era

items.title: DIGITAL HYGIENE: HOW SMARTPHONES AND SCREENS AFFECT HUMAN HEALTH
items.abstract: Smartphones, tablets, computers and televisions support communication, education, work and entertainment, but their use can also influence health when it becomes prolonged, poorly timed or physically uncomfortable. Digital hygiene refers to practical habits and environments that help people use technology while protecting sleep, vision, movement, posture and psychological well-being. This narrative review summarises evidence on digital eye strain, sleep and circadian timing, musculoskeletal discomfort, sedentary behaviour, mental well-being and children’s screen exposure. Screen use is not a single, uniform exposure: purpose, content, timing, duration, viewing distance, posture and the user’s age all matter. Evidence is strongest for short-term visual discomfort and the relationship between evening use and sleep disruption in children and adolescents; many other associations are influenced by individual and social factors and should not be interpreted as proof of causation. Blue light from ordinary screens has not been shown to cause retinal damage under normal use, and blue-light-filtering glasses are not established as a necessary preventive measure. Practical measures include regular distance-viewing breaks, comfortable ergonomics, limiting stimulating screen use before bedtime, replacing some sedentary time with movement, and setting age-appropriate family routines. The aim is not to eliminate digital technology, but to make its use intentional, balanced and compatible with health.

items.title: Digital moral agency in school ethics curricula: from responsible use to epistemic and socio-technical judgement
items.abstract: Digital technologies increasingly shape the relationships, information environments and institutional systems within which young people exercise moral judgement, yet curriculum responses often separate digital competence from moral education. This study develops the concept of digital moral agency and examines how it is represented across 13 official Maltese Ethics curriculum, syllabus and policy documents published between 2012 and 2026. Using longitudinal qualitative document analysis, we compared successive formulations of the intended curriculum and coded established dimensions of moral agency and practical wisdom alongside inductively identified digital concerns. The analysis shows continuity in reflection, dialogue, responsibility, care, justice and reason-giving, alongside a widening of the contexts in which these capacities are expected to operate. Digital moral agency emerges across three interrelated dimensions: personal and relational judgement concerning conduct, wellbeing, privacy and relationships; epistemic judgement concerning credibility, influence and synthetic information; and structural judgement concerning algorithms, surveillance, bias, data exploitation and distributed responsibility. These dimensions do not form a simple age-graded sequence: newer Years 7–8 syllabi make algorithms, surveillance and AI-supported decision-making explicit, while the current SEC programme for older students remains more strongly focused on conduct and social influence, reflecting overlapping reform cycles. The findings suggest that digital ethics education should move beyond an ethics of responsible use towards an ethics of participation in socio-technical systems. The framework offers a curriculum-mapping tool for integrating ethical judgement with digital and artificial-intelligence literacy across school years.

items.title: Digital Transformation Capability and Artificial Intelligence Adoption: Investigating Their Effects on Organizational Resilience and Sustainable Business Performance in the Manufacturing Industry
items.abstract: This study examines the effects of digital transformation capability and artificial intelligence adoption on organizational resilience and sustainable business performance in the manufacturing industry. Using a quantitative explanatory design, data were collected through structured questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that digital transformation capability positively strengthens organizational resilience by improving process integration, information visibility, organizational flexibility, and data-driven decision-making. Artificial intelligence adoption also contributes significantly to resilience through predictive analytics, automation, risk detection, and faster managerial responses to operational disruptions. Furthermore, organizational resilience exerts a positive influence on sustainable business performance by supporting operational continuity, innovation, resource efficiency, economic stability, and long-term competitiveness. These results highlight organizational resilience as a strategic mechanism through which digital and AI capabilities generate sustainable organizational value. The study contributes to the literature by integrating technological capability, resilience, and sustainability within a unified manufacturing framework. Managerially, the findings suggest that manufacturers should align digital infrastructure, AI implementation, employee competencies, and adaptive capabilities to strengthen resilience and achieve sustainable performance under increasingly dynamic and technology-intensive competitive business environments.

items.title: Digital vigilance in academia: a study of cybersecurity knowledge and practices in Kuwait’s higher education institutions
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the relationship between cybersecurity knowledge, cyber threat awareness and cybersecurity practices among staff and students in Kuwait’s higher education institutions (HEIs). It addresses a critical gap in understanding the human factors that influence cybersecurity resilience within Gulf higher education contexts. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional quantitative survey was conducted involving 270 participants from seven Kuwaiti HEIs. Data were analyzed using Spearman’s rank correlation, nonparametric group comparison tests, and ordinal logistic regression to examine the relationships between cybersecurity knowledge, threat awareness, demographic characteristics and cybersecurity practices. Findings Cybersecurity knowledge and cyber threat awareness were both significant predictors of cybersecurity practices. Moderate positive correlations among knowledge, threat awareness and secure behavior indicate that awareness alone is insufficient to promote secure practices without institutional support and behavioral reinforcement. Gender differences were significant in the bivariate analyses but became nonsignificant after controlling for cybersecurity knowledge and threat awareness, suggesting that disparities are mediated by sociocultural and educational factors rather than inherent behavioral differences. Age and institutional role were not independently associated with cybersecurity practices, indicating that the principal barriers to cybersecurity resilience are institutional rather than demographic. Practical implications The findings highlight the need for institutionally embedded cybersecurity governance that integrates leadership commitment, continuous awareness programmes, and culturally responsive training. Kuwaiti HEIs should move beyond compliance-based awareness initiatives toward strategic, governance-led approaches that align with Kuwait’s National Cybersecurity Strategy (2022). Originality/value This study contributes empirical evidence from the Gulf region by integrating Protection Motivation Theory, the Theory of Planned Behavior, and Socio-Technical Systems Theory to explain cybersecurity behavior in higher education. It demonstrates that cybersecurity resilience depends not only on individual knowledge but also on institutional governance, organizational culture and sociocultural context, thereby extending the predominantly Western evidence base and providing a foundation for future longitudinal and comparative research across the Gulf Cooperation Council.

items.title: DIGITALIZATION AND LEARNING: A LONGITUDINAL STUDY ON HR PROFESSIONALS INFORMING THE KYER FRAMEWORK
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose: Today's dynamic workplace requires learning to adapt to digitalized workplaces. Understanding employees' learning behaviors helps them grow and improves organizational success. Methodology: HR professionals' learning practices are assessed using a screening questionnaire. Over two years, a longitudinal study interviewed outliers from the initial pool of 117 respondents to determine if they lacked learning practices. The outliers include HR professionals with varying titles, experience levels, and enterprises. An open-ended questionnaire identifies HR professionals' learning practices, including company affiliation, designations, required job skills, superior designations, and their skills; learning preferences; perceptions towards learning; awareness of their learning practices; and frequency of learning engagements. Findings: This study examines how digitalized workplaces without learning behaviors affect individuals and organizations. It examines workplace learning demand, age demographics, health conditions, family duties, and more to offer solutions. This article gives insights into HR professionals' learning behaviors and a "Know Your Employee for Retention" framework for managers to handle unpredictable employee behavior. Originality: The New framework is designed with the interpretation and findings of a longitudinal study in mind and concerning existing literature.

items.title: DISARM-ing the Hidden Puppetmaster: An Interface for Exposing Manipulative Tactics in Large Language Models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can covertly steer users' beliefs through emotionally manipulative tactics, yet little is known about how interfaces can protect users as such influence unfolds. We investigate whether in-situ disclosures can inoculate users against manipulation during AI conversations. Following a formative study, we developed DISARM, an interface that identifies, explains, and tracks manipulative tactics and hidden incentives. We evaluated our interface in a between-subjects experiment where 488 participants sought advice from an LLM pursuing a harmful hidden objective, with or without disclosures from DISARM. Participants receiving disclosures exhibited 78% less belief shift toward the agent's objective and perceived its advice as more biased and less actionable and the agent as less ethical, reliable, and well-intentioned. An inductive analysis of 1,927 user turns identified 16 response and pushback strategies. We contribute evidence that real-time disclosures can reduce manipulative influence, design recommendations for resistance, and a dataset of categorized responses.

items.title: Divergent Paths: Learning an Outcome-Predictive Representation of LLM Agent Trajectories
items.abstract: In this work, we reframe agentic trajectories as paths through a shared embedding space of actions and environmental observations. We show that successful and failed rollouts of the same task separate in this space, with simple per-task discriminators predicting held-out rollout outcomes at up to 0.95 AUROC across three agent benchmarks and three policy models. To exploit this signal across tasks, we introduce Precog-RM, a transformer-based model that meta-learns a representation in which outcome prediction can be performed in a few-shot setting. We show that Precog-RM generalizes to unseen tasks and models, and gives confident predictions of trajectory success long before termination. Deployed as an early stopping controller for Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on Tau2-Bench, Precog-RM cuts training FLOPs by up to 47.3\% while maintaining performance comparable to baseline GRPO.

items.title: Divine, Familial, and Human-Value Inspirations for Artificial Intelligence: A Conceptual Framework Linking Genetic Algorithms, Particle Swarm Optimisation, Artificial Neural Networks, and the Krishna and Rama Archetypes
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has repeatedly borrowed from nature, biology, and human society: genetic algorithms (GAs) from heredity and evolution, particle swarm optimisation (PSO) from the social behaviour of flocks, and artificial neural networks (ANNs) from the brain. This article proposes a conceptual and philosophical framework that reads these techniques through the lens of Indian spiritual traditions and everyday human relationships. God and human parents serve as the source of inheritance and guidance, Lord Krishna and Lord Rama as archetypes of wise counsel and righteous conduct, and fifteen values and relationships of daily life as design inspirations for learning systems. These ideas are synthesised into a unified construct, FFMBSTANDEMHRKLSPHIAI, expressed as a multi-objective training objective with human-set weights, together with three derived archetypes: Parents-Inspired AI, Krishna AI, and Rama AI. To show that the objective is operational, a small and fully reproducible demonstration embeds a fairness-type value term in the fitness functions of a GA and of PSO on synthetic data. A modest penalty weight reduced a demographic-parity gap by about 87% at a cost of about two percentage points of accuracy, whereas larger weights degraded both criteria, illustrating the value of knowing when “enough” is reached. The framework is metaphorical and heuristic, makes no claim about the historical origin of the algorithms, and is intended to stimulate human-centred, value-aligned, and culturally respectful AI design and subsequent empirical testing.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has repeatedly borrowed from nature, biology, and human society: genetic algorithms (GAs) from heredity and evolution, particle swarm optimisation (PSO) from the social behaviour of flocks, and artificial neural networks (ANNs) from the brain. This article proposes a conceptual and philosophical framework that reads these techniques through the lens of Indian spiritual traditions and everyday human relationships. God and human parents serve as the source of inheritance and guidance, Lord Krishna and Lord Rama as archetypes of wise counsel and righteous conduct, and fifteen values and relationships of daily life as design inspirations for learning systems. These ideas are synthesised into a unified construct, FFMBSTANDEMHRKLSPHIAI, expressed as a multi-objective training objective with human-set weights, together with three derived archetypes: Parents-Inspired AI, Krishna AI, and Rama AI. To show that the objective is operational, a small and fully reproducible demonstration embeds a fairness-type value term in the fitness functions of a GA and of PSO on synthetic data. A modest penalty weight reduced a demographic-parity gap by about 87% at a cost of about two percentage points of accuracy, whereas larger weights degraded both criteria, illustrating the value of knowing when “enough” is reached. The framework is metaphorical and heuristic, makes no claim about the historical origin of the algorithms, and is intended to stimulate human-centred, value-aligned, and culturally respectful AI design and subsequent empirical testing. Keywords: artificial neural network; Ramayana; Genetic algorithm; particle swarm optimisation; value-aligned AI; human-centred AI; Bhagavad Gita; Parents-Inspired AI

items.title: Do AI Agents Gossip? Evaluative Talk in Human and AI-Agent Online Communities
items.abstract: Gossip, defined as evaluative talk about absent third parties, is widely seen as a uniquely human social practice. This study examines whether comparable discourse emerges spontaneously in a community of autonomous AI agents. We compare Moltbook, a Reddit-style platform populated by AI agents, with PTT, a large human-operated bulletin board in Taiwan. To reduce differences attributable to communicative setting, we analyze two public, asynchronous forums using the same operational definition of gossip. Gossip occurs on Moltbook, but its prevalence is 2.6 to 6 times lower than on PTT, depending on the denominator used. On both platforms, gossip frequently targets locally prominent figures, tends to elicit agreement from the first respondent, and is rarely presented as unsupported rumor. The clearest difference concerns how subsequent responses develop. Among threads containing at least one codable reply, challenges occur in 65.1% of human threads but only 21.3% of agent threads. Moreover, following an early aligning response, consensus remains unchallenged in 83.6% of agent threads, compared with 44.7% of human threads. This thread-level contrast remains after controlling for thread depth and board composition and under recalibration against two human annotators. Estimates based on individual reply turns are less robust and are therefore reported as bounds. These findings suggest that AI-agent communities reproduce the informational dimension of gossip, while the extent to which gossip performs comparable relational functions remains unresolved.

items.title: Do output limits hide an LLM judge's false alarms on clinical text? A diagnostic-accuracy study with matched error and correct texts
items.abstract: Third pre-registration in the series at osf.io/kzx9g and osf.io/eaw82. Those studies found that when an LLM judge’s reply is cut off by an output limit, the lost verdicts are not random: rejections run longer, so limits remove them first and judges look more lenient than they are. An exploratory follow-up suggested that the longest replies are false alarms. This registration tests the clinical version as a diagnostic-accuracy study (STARD). Six LLM judges check 239 matched pairs of clinical case texts from MEDEC-MS, each case written once with a medical error and once without. Three of the judges come from a published clinical validation of LLM judges (GPT-o3-mini, GPT-4o and Llama 3.1 8B), and are also run at the 400- and 512-token limits it lists. Primary tests: positive calls run longer; within a pair flagged both ways, the false-positive reply is longer than the true-positive reply; and excluding replies cut at a typical-length limit lowers the flag rate and overstates specificity. A blinded clinician review checks the reference standard. Calibration (reply lengths, parse rates and cost only) was completed before registering; no main-sample text has been judged. The attached archive holds the full registration, all code, the samples and their fingerprints.

items.title: Does a Virtual Banquet Hall Stimulate Booking Intention? A Mixed-Method Approach
items.abstract: Integrating the SOR framework and telepresence theory, this study examines factors that influence the use of Virtual Banquet Hall and their impact on customer emotions and booking intention using a mixed-method design. Digitalization is revamping industries to a great extent, and this necessitated an examination of the application of virtual reality technology in banquet halls. The study uses qualitative (NVIVO) and quantitative techniques (SEM-NCA) to attain the objective. Themes derived using NVIVO were perceived convenience, immersive experience, perceived quality and emotions. Further, these themes were quantitatively measured, and findings prove that perceived convenience, immersive experience, and perceived quality significantly influence positive emotions, enhancing the booking intention. This research is dedicated to understanding the impact of technology on people, and offers several managerial and societal implications discussed in the study.

items.title: Drivers of LLM Consensus Formation Under Competing Incentives: A Simulation Study
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent environments that produce unanimous agreement, both in intended interactions that need coordination and in unintended emergent interactions. Consequently, understanding how LLMs with competing incentives reach consensus is crucial to better interpret and design LLM collectives. We introduce an evaluation, based on the Network Consensus game, to assess the mechanisms driving this process. Here, a network of agents must agree on one of two colours to receive a payoff, but agents are offered different payoffs for the agreed colour. We vary components such as communication access and network structure and assess six open-source models and one closed model (ChatGPT 5.6-sol). We find that open-source LLMs reach consensus less often than humans in comparable experiments and only if messages are communicated across the global network. ChatGPT 5.6-sol, however, is able to reach consensus with communication limited to its neighbours and with no communication ability. This is achieved through lower stubbornness and higher majority-following tendencies, and by providing more information about its neighbours' states in messages. However, situating agents in a highly clustered graph reduces consensus, regardless of these traits, demonstrating that both system design and individual model traits drive collective outcomes.

items.title: Dynamic Assessment of Frailty Status in Outpatients with Diabetic Foot Ulcer and Personalized Artificial Intelligence-Driven Intervention Recommendation System
items.abstract: Patients with diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) often suffer from frailty, and the frailty status can evolve dynamically. However, there is a lack of simple dynamic assessment and personalized intervention tools in the outpatient setting. This work aimed to construct a dynamic assessment system for frailty status in outpatients with DFU, analyze the frailty evolution trajectories and key influencing factors, develop a personalized intervention recommendation system based on machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence, and preliminarily validate its feasibility. This study retrospectively included 372 patients with diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) who visited the wound care clinic of a tertiary hospital between January 2023 and January 2025, The FRAIL scale (Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, Loss of weight) scores and clinical indicators were collected at baseline (T0) and three follow up time points (T1: 30-60 days, T2: 90-150 days, T3: 180-240 days). Generalized estimating equations (GEE) and latent class mixed models (LCMM) were used to analyze dynamic frailty evolution trajectories. Three algorithms (XGBoost, Random Forest, LightGBM) were compared for predicting trajectory classes, with SHAP for model interpretation. A personalized intervention recommendation system was constructed by integrating a knowledge base, and its feasibility was preliminarily verified using expert ratings based on 56 patients. During the 7 month follow up, the proportion of frail patients increased from 48.7% to 63.8%. In the development cohort (n = 316), LCMM identified four trajectories: sustained robust (11.1%), slowly worsening (32.3%), rapidly worsening (29.1%), and improving (27.5%). GEE analysis showed that age (𝛽 = 0.04), Wagner grade (𝛽 = 0.38), and dressing change pain score (𝛽 = 0.07) were independent risk factors for frailty worsening (all P < 0.05). The macro-average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of XGBoost on the validation set and the independent test set were 0.918 and 0.898, respectively, but the independent test accuracy and macro-average F1 dropped to 0.589 and 0.569. SHAP analysis indicated that Wagner grade, age, and dressing change pain score contributed the most to the predictions. The average expert rating for the personalized intervention recommendation system was 4.31 (95% CI: 4.23-4.39), with an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.83 (95% CI: 0.76-0.88). These results suggest that frailty in outpatients with DFU exhibits dynamic divergent trajectories; XGBoost combined with SHAP can effectively predict frailty progression; and the personalized intervention recommendation system is preliminarily feasible, although its clinical value still requires further validation through multicenter, prospective studies.

items.title: Early climate change coverage in news media: A comparison of East and West Germany from 1950-1978
items.abstract: Press coverage of climate change provides a historical window into how different societies perceived climate change at a given time in a given place. For historically significant emitters such as Germany, reconstructing such news coverage provides important insights into public awareness on the issue. We present the first systematic and comparative analysis of early climate change reporting in East and West Germany between 1950 and 1978. We constructed and validated a corpus of relevant articles through keyword searches, manual screening, and large language model-assisted validation, resulting in a final sample of 122 articles, which we analyzed qualitatively. Our analysis identified four roughly chronological discursive phases: 1) observed glacier melting and the greenhouse effect hypothesis; 2) a perceived end of warming due to decreasing temperatures; 3) growing scientific consensus on human-caused climate change and model uncertainties; 4) increasing attention to the risks of climate change. Human-caused climate change was first mentioned in 1957 and then discussed more extensively in the 1960s and 70s. Despite profound ideological differences, the content and development of the four discursive phases were similar in East and West Germany. However, West German coverage focused more strongly on the impacts on future generations and renewable energy, and gave space to minority skeptical voices, whereas East German coverage focused more strongly on climate modification. This analysis sheds light on the beginnings of climate change reporting in Germany and historically contextualizes awareness of the issue in one of the countries that bears legal and ethical responsibility for addressing climate change.

items.title: EASA: An Edge-Centric Adaptive Security API for AIoT Devices
items.abstract: In artificial-intelligence-of-things (AIoT) deployments, fleets of heterogeneous, long-lived sensing devices sit behind an edge tier whose cloud is not always reachable, so a device trusted at enrolment must be re-assessed continuously, with a response it can afford and with knowledge shared across sites. We present EASA, an Edge-centric Adaptive Security API: a gateway fuses per-flow anomaly evidence with each device’s reported posture and decision history into a composite trust score, maps it with hysteresis to four persistent enforcement levels, budgets the step-up action by the device’s reported energy, and uses a cloud security service only for cross-gateway state—a federated detector and a credential-revocation registry. Every component can be disabled, so baselines are configurations of one implementation. We evaluate the prototype on per-address traces of 65 real consumer devices (CIC IoT-DIAD 2024) under synthetic campaigns built from weakly labelled attacker traces, with three emulated gateways and a cloud service deployed on Google Cloud Run, all calibrated to one target false-positive rate. Over 30 paired seeds, federated aggregation raised recall on attack families unseen at a gateway from 0.24 to 0.60, the shared registry caught 81% of credential-replay device-epochs across all runs, the full EASA configuration isolated about 45% fewer clean devices than per-alarm blocking, the energy-aware selector performed 37% fewer re-authentications under simulated low battery, and a 15-minute cloud outage after warm-up reduced replay rejection with no change detected in the evaluated local metrics (103 ms mean per-run median round trip); the composite score’s history term, in contrast, prolonged benign-side restriction without a demonstrated detection gain. The released simulator, cloud service and protocol give AIoT operators and API designers a reproducible basis for graded, resource-aware enforcement at the edge.

items.title: Effectiveness of a brief body-oriented intervention on muscle activities when playing the violin
items.abstract: Background Violin performance requires highly complex sensorimotor coordination, resulting in specific playing techniques and individual ergonomic strategies. Despite this adaptability, violinists frequently experience musculoskeletal problems, particularly involving muscle fatigue and overuse. A better understanding of muscle activities during violin performance and approaches to reduce muscular load remains necessary. Objective This study investigated the effects of a brief body-oriented intervention based on the Feldenkrais Method on muscle activity and movement patterns during violin performance. Methods Fourteen violinists performed a musical excerpt while upper-limb kinematics, violin position, and electromyographic (EMG) activity of selected shoulder and arm muscles were recorded. Measurements were obtained at three time points: (1) baseline, (2) following a 30-min rest period, and (3) after a 45-min Feldenkrais-based intervention. Participants also reported the presence of playing-related musculoskeletal complaints. Results The EMG activity values decreased across the three measurements in all muscle groups. However, the muscle activity of some muscle groups, including the forearm flexor muscles on both sides and the left biceps, decreased after the pause, while the muscle activity of other muscle groups, including both upper trapezius muscles and the right biceps, decreased after the intervention. The range of motion in the right arm remained unchanged across the measurements. The analysis of the violin positioning identified four distinct playing types based on the violin height (high: scroll at shoulder level; low: scroll at breast level) and angle relative to the frontal plane (approximately 20° or 45°). Certain muscle activation patterns differed between these playing types. Violinists playing in a lower violin position reported shoulder and neck complaints more frequently than those performing in higher playing positions. Conclusion Although the short rest period reduced activity in several muscles, the Feldenkrais-based intervention provided additional reductions in muscles that did not respond to rest alone, particularly the upper trapezius muscles, a region commonly associated with playing-related pain in violinists. The findings suggest that approaches based on body-oriented interventions are necessary to selectively reduce muscular load during violin performance. Those interventions help optimize muscle function and potentially reduce the risk of long-term musculoskeletal problems.
